answer: To mint a second identity, an attacker must post a fresh stake and pass a costly attestation, and the atlas of all bonds is published each epoch so duplicates stand out. Participants stake tokens at a registered jetty, a bonded gateway that maps one identity to one hardware-rooted key. A comet score weights each bond by age, so cheap throwaway identities earn near-zero trust. Duplicating one honest agent thus costs a full independent stake plus attestation fees, making sybils economically irrational. In practice, sa0014 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
